IMF Monitor publishes research data on the International Monetary Fund: the conditions in its lending, its programs, its Executive Board, and its technical assistance. It began in 2017 with the first release of the [Conditionality](../conditionality/index.qmd) dataset, and is directed by Thomas Stubbs at Royal Holloway, University of London.

## Independence

IMF Monitor is an independent academic project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or funded by the International Monetary Fund, and its datasets are not official IMF data. "IMF" and "International Monetary Fund" are used only to identify the subject of its research, and the site uses no IMF seal, logo, or other mark.

If you hold rights in anything on this site, or have a concern about how a name or mark is used, please contact Thomas Stubbs at [thomas.stubbs@rhul.ac.uk](mailto:thomas.stubbs@rhul.ac.uk) so that it can be addressed.

## Funding

- The Institute for New Economic Thinking (INET) supported the [Conditionality](../conditionality/index.qmd) dataset with grant INO13-00020.
- The Centre for Business Research at Cambridge Judge Business School funded updates to the Conditionality dataset through a Cambridge Political Economy Society Trust (CPEST) grant.
- The Cambridge-INET Institute (now the Janeway Institute) at the University of Cambridge provided seed funding for the Executive Board minutes data, published here as the [Governance](../governance/index.qmd) dataset.
- The Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC), part of UK Research and Innovation, funded the [Technical Assistance](../technical-assistance/index.qmd) dataset through grant [ES/V012916/1](https://gtr.ukri.org/projects?ref=ES%2FV012916%2F1).
